$comment: The heartbeat's one launch spec, for every runner (HBT-002): the orchestrator entry's prompt is the only prompt any runner gives it. BAXTER reads this file as its manifest (one entry, its schedule, model and timeout) and never writes it: dear-me is "stamp_manifest": false in its repos.json. The Claude routine's own prompt only points here (runners.claude-routine.prompt). Everything the run does is in .claude/jobs/README.md, never here.

heartbeats.name: orchestrator
heartbeats.prompt: You run unattended, with no one present. Open .claude/jobs/README.md in this repository, read it whole, and follow it exactly, from step 0.
heartbeats.description: Starts dear-me's one heartbeat (HBT-002, HBT-006): .claude/jobs/README.md, the orchestrator, which runs the inline jobs and every due job in .claude/jobs/, and stands down when a run is already going or nothing is due.

runners._what: How each runner starts the orchestrator entry above. Its timer lives with the runner; this records what it should be. Only the runner marked "sends": true runs the inline jobs (reminders, check-ins), so two runners never send the same message.

baxter._backup: A-177: sends only the reminders the routine has left this long, each claimed on main first; needs TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN and TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID in BAXTER's own environment, never in the repository

claude-routine.where: a Claude Code routine in the Claude app
claude-routine.environment: Heartbeats (the bot key and chat id as environment variables; api.telegram.org allowed)
claude-routine.prompt: You run unattended, with no one present. Open .claude/heartbeats.json in this repository and do exactly what the prompt of its orchestrator entry says.
